title: Overflow and scroll behaviour
learningObjectives: Explain overflow and scroll behaviour and apply it in a practical page layout.

understand.concept: overflow controls what happens when content does not fit an element's padding box. Values include visible, hidden, clip, scroll, and auto. overflow-x and overflow-y can control axes separately, subject to CSS overflow interactions.
understand.whyItMatters: Clipping can hide information or keyboard focus. Use scrolling intentionally, label scroll regions when useful, and test touch and keyboard access. Avoid fixed heights that cut off enlarged text.
understand.analogy: Overflow is what happens when a container receives more content than it can comfortably hold: it can extend, clip, or provide scrolling.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a learning aid; actual sizing and layout follow CSS formatting rules.

explain.narrative: The content exceeds the maximum height, so the region becomes scrollable. The tabindex makes it keyboard focusable.
